subject.title: [BUG] OpenAI Codex errors leak into user chat

question: Should unconfigured-provider failures be silently dropped at the provider/routing boundary, or converted into generic user-visible error copy after the `detail` parser fix lands?
rationale: The formatter bug is narrow, but the issue also asks for silent suppression based on provider credential state, which changes runtime/operator behavior beyond parsing one payload shape.

options.title: Land parser fix first
options.body: Recognize top-level `detail` payloads now, add focused tests, and track unconfigured-provider suppression as a separate explicit policy decision.

options.title: Silently drop unconfigured-provider failures
options.body: Suppress those failures before payload building, but require live proof and routing tests so real configured-provider failures are still visible.

options.title: Use generic user-visible copy
options.body: Do not drop provider failures by default; always replace raw details with generic safe copy unless a maintainer approves a narrower silent path.

recommendation.title: Land parser fix first
recommendation.body: Recognize top-level `detail` payloads now, add focused tests, and track unconfigured-provider suppression as a separate explicit policy decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The parser and shared error-formatting seam history points to this owner as the best available reviewer for the narrow fix and follow-up policy routing.
